headline: **52%** OF SPACEX
INCOME IS NOW AI
cover.hook_pick_reason: Number hook using the article's own wording: TechCrunch says AI makes up 52% of SpaceX's income, and slides 1-2 back it up. It says 'income', not 'revenue', because the article does. The myth-flip is softer; the spending hook is vague; the forecast hook rests on one Musk prediction. Slide 1 flags that 'income' is TechCrunch's term and gives the $431M AI profit.

slides.title: SpaceX is leaving rocket roots behind
body: SpaceX reported **$14.6B** in Q3 revenue in a regulatory filing on Tuesday. TechCrunch says AI is now **52% of its "income"**, the article's own term. AI profit was $431M.

slides.title: A renamed unit brought in $7.5B
body: The renamed "Super Intelligence" unit generated **$7.5B** in revenue, from the recently acquired Cursor (an AI coding tool), the Grok bot and AI cloud computing. Separately, about $1B of company revenue came from the recovery of Bitcoin prices and unspecified related-party income.

slides.title: AI made $431M, and could have made more
body: The AI business generated **$431M in profit**. It would have been higher without **$1.2B** in one-time stock-based compensation expenses related to the Cursor acquisition.

slides.title: Spending is even bigger: $19.6B
body: Third-quarter capital expenditures hit **$19.6B**, as SpaceX builds a second data center project and invests more in its Starship rocket. CFO Bret Johnsen said it expects to spend **$35B to $40B** on new capital investment in Q4.

slides.title: Profitable again, but not for the year
body: Net income was **$4.4B**, a turnaround from a $1B loss in the same quarter last year. Over the first nine months, SpaceX still had a **$413M net loss**.

slides.title: Musk predicts up to $1 trillion
body: Bullish on the AI business, Elon Musk predicted SpaceX's annual recurring revenue will be "somewhere between **$500 billion and $1 trillion**" by the end of 2027. That is his forecast, not a result. Starlink, its satellite internet service, now serves 13.6M consumers.

facts.text: SpaceX's data centers and Grok agents were more profitable than investors expected in Q3 as the company leaves its roots as a space company behind to focus on AI, which now makes up 52% of its income. (The article says 'income' and does not define it; AI profit was $431M.)
SpaceX reported $14.6 billion in third-quarter revenue on Tuesday, according to its regulatory filing.

The renamed "Super Intelligence" business line generated $7.5 billion in revenue from the recently acquired Cursor coding tool, the Grok bot, and the burgeoning neocloud business. The top-line revenue number was also boosted by about $1 billion in income related to the recovery of Bitcoin prices and unspecified related-party income.
The AI business generated $431 million in profit, which would have been higher without $1.2 billion in one-time stock-based compensation expenses related to the Cursor acquisition.

Total capital expenditures were $19.6 billion (third quarter), as SpaceX builds out a second data center project (Colossus II) and increases investment in Starship, the heavy-lift rocket. CFO Bret Johnsen said the company would spend $35 billion to $40 billion on new capital investments in the fourth quarter.
SpaceX reported net income of $4.4 billion, a turnaround from the $1 billion loss in the same quarter last year. In the first nine months of the year, it still had a net loss of $413 million.

Musk took a bullish stance on the Super Intelligence business segment, predicting annual recurring revenue by the end of 2027 will be "somewhere between $500 billion and $1 trillion." (TechCrunch's sentence says 'SpaceX's annual recurring revenue' in the context of that segment.)

sources.title: SpaceX's AI business is beating expectations

caption:
The rocket company's biggest business is now AI.

SpaceX's third-quarter filing shows $14.6B in revenue, and TechCrunch says AI now makes up 52% of its "income" (its term; AI profit was $431M).

→ The renamed "Super Intelligence" segment brought in $7.5B in revenue (company revenue also got about $1B from the recovery of Bitcoin prices and related-party income)
→ Q3 capital expenditures were $19.6B, with $35B to $40B of new investment expected in Q4
→ Musk predicts SpaceX's annual recurring revenue will be $500B to $1T by the end of 2027 (his forecast, not a result)

Is SpaceX still a space company, or an AI company that builds rockets?

Source: TechCrunch, "SpaceX's AI business is beating expectations", Oct 20, 2026.
